name: Kai Besar White-eye
rangeDescription: Kai besar (kai islands)
description: A small green songbird with a bold white eye-ring and a primarily white underside, except for a yellow throat and base to undertail. Usually found in pairs or singly, roaming through forest, woods, and gardens in lowlands and lower hills.

name: Spotted Bamboowren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais) to northeastern argentina and (?) southeastern paraguay
description: Strange-looking small bird with a slender bill and a rather long tail. Found in bamboo stands in humid forests and second growth where it can be very hard to see.

name: Mussau Triller
rangeDescription: Mussau, in st. matthias group (north-central bismarck archipelago)
description: A rather long-tailed and long-winged bird with a short stubby head, similar in proportions to a small cuckooshrike. Plumage distinctively clean-cut in black and white, with mostly black upperside and white underside, broad white wing panels, and a white rump barred black.

name: River Prinia
rangeDescription: Locally in niger, chad, and northern cameroon (status unknown)
description: An active, slender, unstreaked warbler with a long graduated tail that is sometimes cocked. Gray-brown above and pale below, with a distinctive pale eyebrow.

name: Rufous-winged Buzzard
rangeDescription: Savanna and woodland of southeastern asia, java, and sulawesi
description: A rather small hawk with demonic-looking pale eyes. Grayish-brown with a white belly and warmer cinnamon-brown tones in the wings and tail that are most prominent when the bird is in flight.

name: African Crake
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: Chunky, mid-sized rail. Note the black-and-brown scalloped back, gray head and chest, barred belly, reddish bill and yellowish legs.

name: Fire-fronted Serin
rangeDescription: Mountains of türkiye to western china; winters to israel
description: Sprightly and vividly-colored little finch with a black head and a fiery orange patch on the forehead. Sexes are similar, though female tends to have a smaller forehead patch than the male.

name: Bonaparte's Gull
rangeDescription: Northern north america; winters to mexico and greater antilles
description: The most common small gull through most of North America, especially inland. Breeding adults have a black head, thin white eye arcs, bright red legs, light gray upperparts, and black wingtips.

name: Subtropical Doradito
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to northwestern argentina (south to la rioja)
description: A bright flycatcher found in marshes in the Andes from Colombia to Argentina. Yellow below and olive above, sometimes showing a hint of a dark mask and dull yellowish edges on the wing feathers.

name: Hoary-throated Barwing
rangeDescription: Nepal eastward to bhutan and northeastern india (far western arunachal pradesh) and adjacent china (southern xizang)
description: The combination of this barwing’s pale throat and weak eye-arcs is unique. Found in hill forest with dense understory at approximately 1800-3400 meters of elevation; occasionally lower, especially during the winter.

name: Mountain Bluebird
rangeDescription: Western north america (alaska to central mexico); winters to baja california
description: Adult males are stunning: completely electric turquoise blue with limited white belly. Females are gray with blue wings and tail; some can show a rufous wash on breast.

name: Rosy Starling
rangeDescription: South-central europe; winters primarily india and southeastern arabian peninsula
description: Adult is unique, a vision in glossy black and pale pink. Juvenile is brown with an orange bill.

name: Marsh Warbler
rangeDescription: Europe to central russia; winters to coastal southeastern africa (kwazulu-natal)
description: Medium-sized brown warbler, very similar to Eurasian Reed-Warbler. Best differentiated by the song, which is delightful, distinctive, loud, and full of mimicry of European and African birds.

name: Sabine's Spinetail
rangeDescription: Rainforest of southern guinea to eastern democratic republic of the congo, western uganda, and western kenya
description: A distinctive swift of lowland forest with a square tail and bulging wings that are “pinched” at the body and widest in the center. Wings, back, and throat are blackish, while belly, tail, and rump are white.

name: White-throated Daggerbill
rangeDescription: Both slopes of western andes and west slope of central andes of colombia and west slope of andes of western ecuador
description: Fairly small hummingbird found on the west slope of the Andes from central Colombia to southwestern Ecuador. Both sexes mostly green with short, straight bill.

name: Martial Eagle
rangeDescription: Savanna and thornbush of sub-saharan africa
description: A massive eagle with a short but prominent crest. The adult is uniformly brown on the head, back, and chest, with a pale belly covered in brown blotches.

name: Newton's Fiscal
rangeDescription: São tomé (gulf of guinea); rediscovered 1990 after 50-year absence
description: A long-tailed, upright shrike with black upperparts, a bold white bar on the wing, and yellow-buff underparts. Juvenile is brownish and barred.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Ethiopian Siskin
rangeDescription: Alpine moorlands of northern and central ethiopia
description: An attractive seedeater of the Ethiopian highlands. The distinctive males have a black head and an olive-green and yellow body.

name: Western Chat-Tanager
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern haiti and far southwestern dominican republic (western sierra de bahorucos)
description: A long-tailed, shy, ground-feeding species of wet broadleaf forests with dense undergrowth, especially near streams from 700 to 2,000 meters elevation. Dark brown, with white throat that fades into gray-brown chest and belly.

name: Chestnut-capped Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Campos of interior eastern and south-central brazil to northeastern paraguay
description: Large foliage-gleaner with startling yellow eyes and a long bill and tail. Rather uniform rufous above and paler below.
